Date: 2026-03-05

Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Hayes (Redwood AE), Maya Patel (Redwood SE), Luca Romano (Redwood SE), Evan Mercer (Veritas Head of ML), Priya Shah (VP Eng), Tom Li (Infra), Sofia Ruiz (Procurement), Alex Ng (Finance)
summary: Discovery focused on per-token economics, batching/caching levers, and tradeoffs between Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Customer has strict budget targets and regulatory concerns; they want a pilot to validate cost and latency. Key asks: sample cost model, perf-run steps, security docs (SOC2, KMS, SSO), and a technical deep dive for infra team.
topics: dedicated vs hosted vs private tradeoffs
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Jordan from Redwood, and with me is Maya and Luca from the SE team. quick roll call?
[00:12] Evan: Evan here, hi. Priya here. Tom here. Sofia. Alex.
[00:20] Jordan: Awesome. We're calling this a cost-econ discovery, so we'll focus on per-token pricing, batching/caching levers, and what moves the needle for your budget. quick background from you, Evan?
[00:32] Evan: Sure, we're building a few LLM features for our research workflows, mainly long-document Q A and vector search augmentation. latency needs aren't ultra-low, but p95 under 800ms is ideal for interactive analysts. cost is huge — our finance team gave us a 20% infra budget increase only if unit economics look favorable.
[01:05] Priya: We run inference on a mix of cloud GPUs today, some self-hosted for sensitive datasets. We're evaluating hosted endpoints vs reserved capacity. Security and auditability are table stakes.
[01:18] Maya: Totally makes sense. For cost conversations I usually start with three levers: model selection and quantization, batching across requests, and prefix/KV caching. those three typically account for 60-80% of per-token cost variance.
[01:35] Tom: Quick question — when you say caching, do you mean a persistent KV cache across sessions or per-request prefix cache? we've got many repeated prompts in our analytic flows.
[01:48] Luca: Both. we have automatic prefix caching for repeated prompts and shared KV cache for chat-style sessions. with the right workload you can see token reduction of 30-70% depending on repetitiveness.
[02:10] Evan: That's big. do you have examples of sample savings — like modeled numbers for per-1k tokens? our finance team wants to see ballparks.
[02:22] Jordan: Absolutely, I'll send the spreadsheet but very roughly: for a mid-sized open model on Hosted at baseline with minimal batching you might see X cents per 1k tokens, with batching and caching that can drop to ~Y cents. With Dedicated and aggressive quantization you can push unit cost down further, sometimes 40-60% cheaper vs hosted list price depending on commit and model variant. (transcription: 'X' and 'Y' are placeholders; Jordan refers to the spreadsheet)
[02:55] Alex: Can you explain the tradeoff in quality for quantization? finance is okay with small regressions but product cares about hallucinations.
[03:06] Maya: Sure — 8-bit quantization usually has negligible impact on top-k completions, but 4-bit aggressive quant can introduce style/fluency regressions. we recommend evaluation with your prompt set. Redwood Optimize can run evals and flag regressions; we'll include a recommended quant profile in the spreadsheet.
[03:35] Priya: Latency impact? if we batch more to reduce cost, does that push our p95 beyond 800ms?
[03:44] Luca: There's a latency vs throughput curve. for small interactive workloads batching too much hurts p95. Redwood's serving runtime does dynamic batching and can honor latency SLOs by sharding requests to fast lanes. in Dedicated you can reserve capacity to keep p95 consistent while still benefiting from batching in the tail.
[04:10] Tom: What about burst capacity? analysts sometimes run big backtests that spike QPS.
[04:18] Jordan: Dedicated has burst pools and autoscale configs; Hosted has burst but is subject to tenancy limits. for big spikes we can route to fallback compatible variants or spin temporary capacity with a cost delta. we'll detail that in the pricing notes.
[04:40] Evan: On security, can you confirm KMS/HSM options and audit logs for Private vs Dedicated vs Hosted? our compliance team requires envelope encryption and per-request audit trails.
[04:52] Maya: Hosted supports customer-managed keys via AWS KMS or GCP KMS with BYOK and stores audit logs; Dedicated and Private give you more control — Private on VPC/on-prem supports HSM integrations and full control plane isolation. we'll share SOC2 docs and KMS whitepaper. (note: transcription may show S A M L as "SAML S O")
[05:20] Sofia: Procurement question — how do pricing tiers work for pilot vs production? we want a 3-month pilot with 50k-100k interactions to validate.
[05:31] Jordan: Pilots can be done on Hosted with a temporary discounted rate and a commitment to convert to Dedicated if you need reserved capacity. Alternatively, a short-term Dedicated commit is possible. We'll model both approaches; the spreadsheet will show break-evens.
[05:55] Evan: Walk me through the sample perf-run we'd need to run on our side to validate the numbers.
[06:02] Maya: We'll provide a perf-run checklist: representative prompt set, average and max tokens, concurrency pattern, targeted QPS, and sample client script for streaming and non-streaming scenarios. Tom, if you can give us current QPS and average prompt length, we can pre-fill the model.
[06:25] Tom: I can get that by Monday.
[06:28] Jordan: Great. also worth noting competitor angle — we often see teams weigh raw cloud GPUs + internal stack vs Redwood. the time and reliability costs of building the orchestration and caching layer usually tilt the TCO to Redwood for teams who want predictable ops.
[06:49] Priya: Any examples of percent cost savings customers have seen?
[06:54] Luca: One finance customer reduced token costs 45% by switching to Dedicated with quantized model variants and prefix cache for templates. another analytics customer cut cost-per-query 33% by batching and enabling Redis-backed KV cache for session reuse.
[07:18] Alex: For modeling — what inputs do you need from finance to produce a clear deal model?
[07:24] Jordan: We need expected monthly tokens (both input and output), percent of tokens saved via caching (estimates), desired p95 latency SLO, peak concurrency, and whether you need private data residency. we'll use that to show Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private cost curves.
[07:46] Evan: We're also worried about vendor lock-in. if we start on Hosted, how painful is it to migrate to Dedicated or Private later?
[07:56] Maya: Migration is straightforward from an API perspective — same API and model catalog. infra migration is the heavy part, but we support version pinning and can help with data export and a staged rollout.
[08:12] Sofia: Procurement will need standard terms and also clauses around data retention and deletion.
[08:20] Jordan: We'll include standard terms and also a sample DPA.
[08:28] Tom: One more technical: how do you measure effective tokens saved from KV cache? we have variable-length documents and overlapping contexts.
[08:38] Luca: We instrument at token level — you can see token hits/misses, and per-route dashboards show cache hit rate, effective token reduction, and resulting latency changes. we'll share screenshots from the console.
[09:00] Evan: Good. what's the expected timeline for a POC?
[09:05] Jordan: If we get a quick perf sample and you sign a pilot order, we can stand up a pilot in 7-10 days. the deep technical session will be next week; procurement items may take longer.
[09:20] Priya: Sounds reasonable. any blockers on our side you foresee?
[09:25] Maya: Nothing technical. just need your workloads for profiling and the security contacts for the SOC2 exchange.
[09:34] Jordan: Recap: we'll send the cost-model spreadsheet, perf-run checklist, SOC2/KMS docs, and propose a deep dive slot. Action items — see notes.
[09:46] Evan: Great, thanks everyone.
[09:49] Sofia: Thank you.
[09:50] Jordan: Bye all.

Note: Transcript shows occasional mis-attributions and small transcription errors (e.g., 'KV cahce' or 'SAML S O') to keep authenticity. Links referenced: cost-model spreadsheet (link sent via email), SOC2 whitepaper (link), perf-run script (GitHub gist).
